_table: Key reference rules (repair-and-deduct, illegal-lockout penalty, etc.)
_note: Each state maps to a list of rules; detail / citation may be null; effective_through (ISO date) marks the last known-good date for a volatile figure.
_notice: General reference, not legal advice. Statutes change and vary by jurisdiction; verify every figure against the current official state code before relying on it. Last reviewed 2026-05.

CA.value: Up to one month's rent, no more than twice in any 12-month period
CA.detail: Available after written or oral notice of an untenantable condition the landlord fails to repair in a reasonable time (30 days is presumed reasonable). Not available if the tenant caused the condition.

CA.value: $100 per day, $250 minimum per cause of action, plus actual damages
CA.detail: Self-help eviction (changing locks, shutting off utilities, removing doors or the tenant's belongings) is barred. Repeated, non-contemporaneous violations are separate causes of action with separate awards.

CA.value: Reclaim within 15 days (18 if mailed); under $700 total value, landlord may keep or dispose
CA.detail: After a Notice of Right to Reclaim Abandoned Property (Civ. Code §§ 1983-1985), property over $700 in total resale value must go to public sale with surplus paid to the county (§ 1988).

CA.value: Reciprocal: a one-sided lease fee clause is enforced for whichever party prevails
CA.detail: Even a landlord-only attorney-fee clause entitles a prevailing tenant to fees; the clause is made mutual by operation of law.

CA.value: Capped at the landlord's actual cost; statutory base $30 (1997) indexed to CPI ($65.86 for 2026)
CA.detail: Receipt required; unused portion refundable. The cap is re-indexed each December, so confirm the current-year figure before charging.

FL.value: Actual and consequential damages or 3 months' rent, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees
FL.detail: A landlord may not shut off utilities or block access; repeated, non-contemporaneous violations are separately awarded.

IL.value: Self-help eviction (lockout, utility shutoff) is barred; only the sheriff may evict
IL.detail: Forcible entry is prohibited statewide, but Illinois has no statewide monetary penalty statute; local ordinances such as Chicago's impose penalties.

MA.value: Actual damages or 3 months' rent, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees, and criminal penalties
MA.detail: Willful lockout, utility shutoff, or interference with quiet enjoyment is barred; possession may be regained only by judicial process.

NJ.value: Possession, all damages, court costs, and attorney fees; treble damages where restoring possession is inappropriate
NJ.detail: Self-help eviction is barred; entry into an occupied residence requires the tenant's consent or legal process.

NY.value: Treble damages for a forcible or unlawful eviction
NY.detail: Evicting an occupant who has lived there 30+ days without a court order is also a class A misdemeanor under RPAPL 768.

OR.value: Up to two months' rent or twice the actual damages, whichever is greater
OR.detail: A landlord who unlawfully removes or excludes a tenant, or willfully shuts off an essential service, is liable; the tenant may also get injunctive relief to recover possession.

TX.value: Civil penalty of one month's rent plus $1,000, actual damages, court costs, and attorney fees
TX.detail: A landlord may not lock a tenant out except by judicial process; a lock change for delinquent rent requires written notice and a new key on request.

WA.value: Tenant recovers possession, actual damages, and attorney fees
WA.detail: It is unlawful to remove or exclude a tenant except under a court order; self-help eviction is barred.
